kept.excerpt: Real Madrid were expected to make an offer for Rodri and were believed to have made initial contact with Manchester City, according to Sky Sports News. Madrid were believed willing to pay £43 million–£51 million (€50 million–€60 million), given that he had one year left on his contract. City did not want to sell him and hoped to agree a new long-term contract.
kept.relevance: This late-July report identifies active interest from a prospective buyer while showing that City's stated preference remained retention.

kept.excerpt: AS reported that Rodri prioritized Real Madrid if he left Manchester City, despite interest from Barcelona and other clubs. Barcelona had approached his representatives but had not contacted City, according to SER. City were asking €75 million, while Madrid hoped to complete a deal for around €60 million. Madrid also needed at least one player departure to accommodate its planned signings.
kept.relevance: The cutoff-day report describes the reported destination preference, valuation gap and squad constraints that still stood between interest and a completed transfer.
